summary: `make up` fails on the in-Docker scanner build (typescript@7.0.2), and four tickets have worked around it
description:
`make up` does not work on at least one developer machine. The scanner image's build step fails:

```
> [scanner build 6/6] RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter scanner build
  at getExePath (…/typescript@7.0.2/node_modules/typescript/lib/getExePath.js:53:19)
[ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL] scanner@0.0.0 build: `tsc -b && vite build`
target scanner: failed to solve: … exit code: 1
```

It looks like TypeScript 7's native binary failing to resolve inside the container, but that is a
guess from the stack — **diagnosis is the first half of this ticket.**

**Why it matters more than it looks.** `make up` is what AGENTS.md names for the browser-submit gate:
*"drive the real stack (`make up`) in a browser and submit the write path."* With it broken, four
tickets (TKT-220 through TKT-223) each verified against a **smoke-shaped stack** built from host
artifacts (`compose.smoke.yaml`) instead. That worked and it is not the same thing: the smoke path
ships host-built binaries, so the in-Docker build is exactly the surface nobody is exercising.

`make check` passes throughout, because its smoke stage uses the same fast path.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `make up` completes on a clean checkout, or the failure is diagnosed and the fix is applied
  wherever it belongs (scanner's Dockerfile, the pinned TypeScript, or the pnpm workspace).
- [ ] The finding says whether this is **host-local or real** — if it only reproduces on arm64 macOS,
  say so, because that changes who is affected and whether CI would ever have caught it.
- [ ] If the fix is not obvious, the ticket may land as a **documented workaround plus a diagnosis**
  rather than a repair — but it must not land as silence.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed BEFORE the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** replacing the smoke fast path (`compose.smoke.yaml` is deliberate and stays) ·
TKT-196's browser harness, which is a different problem that this one makes harder.

objective.note: `make up` works, or its failure is understood and written down.

scope.note: One build step in one image. It does not touch the smoke fast path.

uncertainties.note: The cause is a guess from a stack trace; diagnosis is the ticket's first half. It may turn out to be host-local, which is a legitimate outcome and changes the fix.

approach.note: Reproduce, read the container build log, bisect between the pinned TypeScript, the Dockerfile's node base and the pnpm workspace resolution.

first_slice.note: The whole thing is one slice; it is small.

success.note: `make up` exits 0 and the stack becomes healthy — or a written diagnosis with a reproducer.

binding.rule: A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. ... For any back-office/storefront/scanner ticket that adds or changes a write form, drive the real stack (`make up`) in a browser and submit the write path, not just the render.
Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored.

governingAdrs.why: One version per shared dependency declaration. If the fix is a TypeScript version change it has to move everywhere at once, and check-dep-drift enforces that.

reference.summary: The workaround four tickets used, and why it is not equivalent: scripts/smoke.sh's fast path builds artifacts on the HOST and mounts them (compose.smoke.yaml), so the in-Docker build path is exactly what stops being exercised.
The gate this breaks is named in AGENTS.md and in TKT-196; it is the one that caught guest checkout 403ing behind a new bridge and three driver-level SQL defects during TKT-220..223.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness — PASS

Small, isolated, no product risk, and the one uncertainty (the cause) is the work rather than a
blocker. `risk:low` is **not** claimed: the fix may touch a pinned dependency, and ADR-035 makes that
a repo-wide change rather than a local one.

**Verdict:** PASS.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-227

Running **gateless per `config.gates: autonomous`**. Gate 1 (Backlog → Ready) was taken by the
owner's instruction to "take from backlog and start the work"; the ticket's `readiness` verdict was
already **PASS** with all eight DoR items met (one `deferred`, the cause, which is the work itself).

**Backend:** local tracker (`config.tracker: "local"`).
**Branch:** `TKT-227-make-up-in-docker-build` off `origin/main`.

**Selection reason:** the owner named it. It is also the ticket that unblocks the browser-submit
gate AGENTS.md makes mandatory for web-UI work — four tickets (TKT-220..223) already shipped
verified against the smoke-shaped stack instead, so the debt is compounding.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` is NOT claimed.** Stated explicitly rather than left silent, per the
label's carve-outs: the shaping comment refused it because the fix might move a pinned dependency
(ADR-035 makes that repo-wide). Diagnosis has since changed the reason but not the verdict — the
defect is in **credential bootstrap** (`scripts/env-bootstrap.sh`), which is squarely inside the
"auth / secrets" carve-out. The plan gate stays.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — by `gpt-5.6-luna` (config.models.plan), via the codex companion, read-only

**Diagnosis handed to the drafter (executed by the orchestrator, not reasoned):**

- The reported **TypeScript 7 / `getExePath` scanner failure does not reproduce.** Clean
  `--no-cache` builds of `web/scanner/Dockerfile` succeed on `linux/amd64` **and** on emulated
  `linux/arm64`, and also at `a9b81de5` — the exact commit that was HEAD when the ticket was filed.
  Mechanism understood: TS7 resolves a native binary from an optional dep
  `@typescript/typescript-<os>-<cpu>`; `getExePath.js` throws the reported error only when none is
  on disk. In-container, `@typescript/typescript-linux-x64@7.0.2` installs and `tsc --version`
  reports 7.0.2.
- **`make up` nevertheless fails, reproducibly, for an unrelated reason.** It never reaches an
  image build: compose interpolation dies on `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`, required with `:?` at
  `compose.yaml:207` and `:473`, and **never generated by `scripts/env-bootstrap.sh`**. The compose
  error message tells the developer to *"run `make up` once to generate a local credential"* — which
  is self-referentially false. Introduced by **TKT-244** (`720bfc58`), which added the requirement
  without extending the bootstrap.
- **Why the gate never caught it:** `make check`'s smoke path sources `scripts/stack-env.sh`, which
  *does* generate the token (lines 84–86, deliberately an independent fifth draw). The two env
  paths diverged and only the smoke one is in the gate. Counted mechanically: `compose.yaml` marks
  **19** distinct variables required; `env-bootstrap.sh` produces **18**. The gap is exactly one.

The drafter was given the ticket, the COS, the governing ADRs, the governing tests from AGENTS.md,
and was asked to challenge the diagnosis. It read the real tree and surfaced three seams the
orchestrator had missed (`scripts/gate-selftest.sh`, the existing 2026-08-07 learning, and stale
claims in `scripts/browser.sh` / `docs/demo-readiness.md`).

---

# TKT-227 Execution Plan

## Scope decision

Land three things:

1. Repair the reproducible `make up` failure by adding `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` to [`scripts/env-bootstrap.sh`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/scripts/env-bootstrap.sh:72), using its own `/dev/urandom` draw.
2. Add a shell/Compose regression guard proving that a fresh bootstrap satisfies every `${VAR:?}` requirement in [`compose.yaml`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/compose.yaml:32).
3. Update the existing TypeScript diagnosis in [`docs/learnings/2026-08-07-a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/docs/learnings/2026-08-07-a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md:15), including that the actual current `make up` failure was bootstrap drift, not TypeScript.

Do not change the TypeScript pin, lockfile, smoke fast path, or web Dockerfiles. The TypeScript failure does not reproduce on the tested Linux architectures or historical commit. The Dockerfile inconsistencies are real but unrelated to the observed failure and should become a follow-up covering all three web Dockerfiles and the hermetic workflow’s path filters.

Also update the stale explanation in [`scripts/browser.sh`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/scripts/browser.sh:31) and related documentation so the browser gate is described as intentionally smoke-shaped, not as a workaround for a known scanner failure.

No new ADR is required. The repair follows ADR-057’s existing credential decision and ADR-059’s existing generation convention. ADR-035 requires no dependency change.

## Test seam

There is no existing direct test for `env-bootstrap.sh` or `stack-env.sh`. The closest precedent is [`scripts/gate-selftest.sh`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/scripts/gate-selftest.sh:1), which uses disposable worktrees, positive controls, and deliberate mutations.

Add a new shell test at `scripts/env-bootstrap-test.sh` and invoke it from a new `check-env-bootstrap` target in [`Makefile`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/Makefile:17).

The test must:

- run against a disposable copy/worktree;
- remove any `.env` before bootstrapping;
- unset relevant host environment variables so the fixture cannot pass accidentally;
- execute `scripts/env-bootstrap.sh`;
- run `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.direct-ports.yaml config`, without starting containers;
- avoid printing generated credential values;
- assert the inventory token is present and distinct from `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`;
- verify a second bootstrap preserves existing values.

Invariant:

> After a fresh local bootstrap, every configuration value marked mandatory by the development stack is available and valid before the stack is resolved.

This tests the shell and Compose boundary where the defect exists, rather than a Go fake or smoke-only environment.

## Files to touch

- `scripts/env-bootstrap.sh` — add `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` to the opaque-token generation loop and document its independent blast radius.
- `scripts/env-bootstrap-test.sh` — new executable regression test for fresh bootstrap, Compose interpolation, credential separation, and idempotence.
- `Makefile` — add `check-env-bootstrap` and include it in `make check`.
- `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` — add a clean-baseline case and a mutation deleting the inventory token generation; the new test must fail on that mutation.
- `docs/development.md` — document the inventory staff credential alongside the existing generated credentials and explain that it is distinct from the shared internal token.
- `docs/learnings/2026-08-07-a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md` — record the final TypeScript diagnosis and the separate bootstrap root cause.
- `docs/LEARNINGS.md` — update the index entry.
- `scripts/browser.sh` — remove the stale claim that the scanner Docker build is broken.
- `docs/demo-readiness.md` — remove the stale statement that the browser path is routed around `make up` because of TKT-227.

Do not modify `compose.smoke.yaml`; its independently generated token is already correct.

## Definition of done

- `make up` succeeds from a fresh checkout with no `.env`, including the scanner image build and service health checks.
- `make down` cleans up the verification stack; no database-volume behavior changes are introduced.
- `make check` passes.
- `make smoke-hermetic` passes, confirming the in-Docker path independently of the fast smoke path.
- The new regression test fails against the unfixed bootstrap omission and passes after the repair.
- Generated output is checked before the final gate; any regenerated files are committed before running `make check`.
- Documentation clearly states:
  - TypeScript 7.0.2 was not reproduced in the tested environments;
  - the likely failure mode is a platform/store/optional-dependency installation issue;
  - the actual reproducible `make up` defect was the missing bootstrap credential.

## Test plan

1. **Fresh bootstrap satisfies Compose**

   Assert that a clean disposable environment can run bootstrap and `docker compose ... config` successfully.

   Make it red by deleting `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` from the generation loop. Compose must fail with the same missing-variable error.

2. **Credential separation**

   Assert that the generated inventory token is non-empty, has the expected generated length, and differs from `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`.

   Make it red by replacing the inventory draw with the internal token.

3. **Existing `.env` preservation**

   Seed an unrelated `.env` entry and an existing inventory token, run bootstrap twice, and assert that both remain unchanged.

   Make it red by removing the `needs_generation` guard or changing `env_set` to overwrite existing values.

4. **Gap demonstration**

   Before wiring the new guard into `make check`, run the new test against the current unfixed tree with `.env` absent and capture its failure. Run the existing smoke/check path separately and confirm it remains green because [`scripts/stack-env.sh`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/scripts/stack-env.sh:78) already supplies the token. Then apply the bootstrap repair and rerun the regression successfully.

5. **Gate self-test**

   Extend [`scripts/gate-selftest.sh`](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/scripts/gate-selftest.sh:36) with:

   - a positive control proving the clean bootstrap test passes;
   - a mutation removing the inventory generation line;
   - an assertion that `check-env-bootstrap` fails.

## Risks and follow-ups

- Existing developer `.env` files are preserved. A missing inventory token adds one line; an existing value is not rotated.
- If a developer manually configured the inventory token equal to `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`, bootstrap will leave it unchanged and inventory will correctly refuse to start. Documentation should explain removing or replacing the conflicting value.
- The token is not stored in a Docker volume. `make down`’s `-v` behavior remains unchanged and is unrelated to this repair.
- CI requires no new secret. `make check` already runs in CI, and the smoke/browser stack uses `stack-env.sh`.
- No browser spec is needed because this ticket changes no form or browser write path.
- The web Dockerfile differences should be tracked separately: scanner filtering/copy scope, the stale back-office Node image, and hermetic workflow coverage for `web/backoffice/Dockerfile`.

## Challenge to the supplied diagnosis

The executed observations are consistent, but “host-local” is stronger than the evidence proves. Clean Linux `amd64` and emulated `arm64` builds rule out a straightforward repository or architecture defect, but they do not prove the original failure was specifically macOS-local. The accurate conclusion is:

> The TypeScript failure was not reproduced in the tested clean Linux environments, and is most plausibly environment-specific—likely an incomplete optional dependency installation or platform-mismatched pnpm store.

The claim that the scanner workspace shape is an inconsistency is valid, but it does not itself explain the failure. `--frozen-lockfile` validates the importers discovered in the image; it does not require every workspace importer to be copied into the Docker build context.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Plan critique — by `main-agent` (config.models.planReview)

Cross-model invariant holds: drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna`, critiqued by `main-agent`. Every file,
symbol and ADR the draft names was checked to exist at HEAD (`git grep -n` / direct read); the
draft hallucinated **nothing** — `scripts/gate-selftest.sh`, `docs/learnings/2026-08-07-…md`,
`docs/development.md`, `docs/demo-readiness.md`, `scripts/browser.sh`, `compose.smoke.yaml`,
ADR-057 and ADR-059 are all real. That is unusual and worth recording.

#### ACCEPT — the scope decision

Repair the bootstrap, document the TypeScript diagnosis, defer the Dockerfile inconsistencies.
Correct. The ticket's COS #3 explicitly licenses "documented workaround plus a diagnosis", and
COS #1's "or the failure is diagnosed" is satisfied by a *reproducible* repair of the thing that
actually breaks `make up`.

#### ACCEPT — the challenge to my diagnosis, with the wording amended

The drafter is right that **"host-local" overstates the evidence**. I ruled out the repository and
the architecture axis; I did not prove macOS-specificity, and I cannot from this box. Adopting the
drafter's wording for COS #2 verbatim. This is the honest answer, and per AGENTS.md — *a security
(here, a diagnosis) claim is a hypothesis until it is executed* — the executed part is the
non-reproduction, not the attribution.

#### AMEND 1 (material) — the guard must not need Docker

The draft's `scripts/env-bootstrap-test.sh` runs `docker compose ... config`. **This is the one
change that would stop it being a standing guard.**

I first read `gate-selftest.sh` as manual-only and was wrong: `.github/workflows/check.yaml` runs
it as its **own CI job** (`gate-selftest`, line 60). So extending it *does* create a standing
guard — the draft's step 5 is stronger than I initially credited. But that job installs Go, pnpm
and Node and **no Docker**, and `make check` itself never calls `docker compose config` outside the
smoke stage. A Docker-dependent assertion would be skipped or red there.

It is also unnecessary. The requirement set is recoverable by parsing `compose.yaml` directly, and
I executed the comparison:

```
required:  grep -oE '\$\{[A-Z_]+:\?[^}]*\}' compose.yaml | sed 's/\${//;s/:?.*//' | sort -u   → 19 vars
generated: run env-bootstrap.sh on an empty .env, then read back the keys              → 18 vars
comm -23 required have                                                                 → INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN
```

It names **exactly** the defect and nothing else, with no Docker, in milliseconds. Build the guard
on that.

#### AMEND 2 — state the invariant without naming the implementation

The draft's invariant sentence mentions "Compose". Per AGENTS.md (*a green test can bless the
defect* — say the rule without naming the mechanism), use:

> **Every credential the development stack refuses to start without is produced by the one command
> a developer is told to run.**

That phrasing is what makes the guard catch the *next* TKT-244 rather than this one. Derive the
expected set from the requirement (`compose.yaml`'s `:?` markers), never from a run — an assertion
written by observing what `env-bootstrap.sh` currently emits would pin the defect as correct.

#### AMEND 3 — the gap demonstration is mandatory and must be recorded

The draft has it (step 4) and it is right, but AGENTS.md makes it non-negotiable for a
coverage-gap ticket: **one run where the new guard goes red against the unfixed tree and the
pre-existing guards stay green.** Capture both halves in the coding stage comment, not just the
green end state. Concretely: guard red with the bootstrap line absent; `make check` green in the
same state (it will be — `stack-env.sh` supplies the token for smoke), which is precisely the
divergence being closed.

#### AMEND 4 — one seed, one mechanism

The draft's test list (fresh-bootstrap, credential separation, idempotence) is good, but AGENTS.md's
*fixture that seeds N mechanisms* rule applies: for **each** assertion, state what deleting it turns
red. Specifically, the "distinct from `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`" assertion is not decoration — it is
load-bearing, because `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:133` refuses to start on equality,
and `scripts/stack-env.sh:78-86` documents that the back office refuses to boot when it equals
either credential it already holds. A shared draw would satisfy "is present" and still not boot.

#### REJECT — adding a new `check-env-bootstrap` target to `make check`

Not because the check is wrong, but because it duplicates a seam that already exists and is already
in CI. Put the mutation in `gate-selftest.sh` (where `expect_fail`/`expect_pass` already implement
AGENTS.md's delete-the-mechanism-and-re-run discipline in disposable worktrees) and keep the
assertion itself in one script. Adding a target to `make check` for a check that runs in
milliseconds and is already covered by the selftest job buys a second place to keep in sync — and
divergence between two env paths is the *exact* defect this ticket exists to close. Do not
introduce a third.

If the reviewer at Gate 3 disagrees, the cheap version is `check-env-bootstrap` as its own target
invoked *by* the selftest, not by `make check`.

#### CONFIRM — a finding the draft surfaced that I had missed, now corroborated

`docs/demo-readiness.md:87-95` **already records** that TKT-227 did not reproduce on this box, and
asks for the ticket to be corrected because `scripts/browser.sh:32` is routed around `make up` on
its authority. The dates close the argument:

| date | event |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-06 | TKT-227 filed: scanner build fails |
| 2026-08-10 | `demo-readiness.md`: `make up` **worked**, scanner image built cleanly with TS 7.0.2 |
| 2026-08-15 | **TKT-244** (`720bfc58`) adds the `:?` requirement without touching `env-bootstrap.sh` |
| 2026-08-17 | `make up` fails — on the credential, never reaching a build |

Two different failures five days apart, and the board attributes both to the first. Fixing
`scripts/browser.sh:32` is therefore **in scope**, not cosmetic: it is a live comment asserting a
broken build as the reason for a gate detour, and it is false.

#### Pre-mortem — how this ticket ships and is still wrong

1. **The guard passes because the fixture has a `.env`.** The single most likely failure. The test
   must run with `.env` absent *and* with the host's own env unset — otherwise it asserts against a
   tree already carrying the value and can never reach the failing state.
2. **The fix is verified only by `make check`.** `make check` is green **right now**, with the
   defect live. Green there proves nothing about this ticket; the evidence is `make up` reaching a
   healthy stack, plus the red-then-green guard run.
3. **`make up` is verified on this box and this box has the port problem.** `demo-readiness.md`
   documents Docker Desktop/WSL2 returning 500 on `127.0.0.1:5432` and `:8080`. If `make up` fails
   *after* the credential fix, check that before concluding the fix is wrong — and use
   `GATEWAY_PORT`/`POSTGRES_PORT` overrides, which are config-only.
4. **Rotation surprise.** `needs_generation` treats empty-or-retired as regenerate. A developer
   whose `.env` already has the token keeps it; one who set it equal to `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`
   keeps a value inventory will refuse to boot on. Document the remedy; do not silently rotate.

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Per the skill's required section — design elements **added** here rather than accepted/amended from
the draft, which therefore reach Gate 2 reviewed by nobody but their author:

1. **The Docker-free `compose.yaml` `:?` parse as the guard's mechanism** (AMEND 1). I executed it
   and it returns exactly the one missing variable, but the *design choice* to parse compose text
   rather than ask Compose is mine alone. Its known weakness: it reads `${VAR:?}` syntax literally,
   so a requirement expressed another way (a required var introduced via an `env_file`, or `:?`
   written across a line break) would be invisible to it. I judge that acceptable — every one of
   the 19 current requirements uses this exact form — but it is unreviewed.
2. **Dropping the `make check` target** (REJECT above) in favour of the existing selftest seam.
3. **The invariant sentence** in AMEND 2.

Flagging these again at the Gate 2 hand-off, as the skill requires.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan final — delta on the `kind=plan` draft

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Not restated; read the two together.

Running gateless (`config.gates: autonomous`), so Gate 2 is taken here. Every open decision is
resolved below, each one adopting the critique's recommendation — no decision needed the
most-reversible tiebreak.

#### Decisions taken (agent, in place of the human at Gate 2)

1. **Guard mechanism: Docker-free `compose.yaml` parse.** Adopted from AMEND 1. Rationale: the CI
   `gate-selftest` job has Go/pnpm/Node and no Docker, so a `docker compose config` assertion could
   not stand there. Executed before deciding — the parse returns exactly
   `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` against the current tree.
2. **No new `make check` target.** Adopted from REJECT. The assertion lives in one script, seeded
   and mutation-checked from `scripts/gate-selftest.sh`, which already runs as its own CI job.
   Rationale: this ticket exists because two env paths diverged; adding a third place to keep in
   sync would be the same mistake in a new costume.
3. **COS #2 answered as "not reproduced", not "host-local".** Adopted from ACCEPT-2. The
   non-reproduction is executed fact; macOS attribution is not, and will not be asserted.
4. **Dockerfile inconsistencies → follow-up ticket, not this one.** Adopted from the draft's scope
   decision. They are real (scanner's missing `--filter`, back-office's stale `node:26.5.0`) but
   caused none of the observed failures, and folding an unforced Dockerfile change into a
   credential fix widens the blast radius of a ticket that is already on an auth path.
5. **`scripts/browser.sh:32` and `docs/demo-readiness.md` corrections are IN scope.** Adopted from
   CONFIRM. A live comment asserting a broken build as grounds for a gate detour is false and
   load-bearing; leaving it is the "lands as silence" outcome COS #3 forbids.

#### Amendments folded in

- AMEND 2 — the invariant, implementation-free: *every credential the development stack refuses to
  start without is produced by the one command a developer is told to run.* The expected set is
  derived from `compose.yaml`'s `:?` markers (the requirement), never from what
  `env-bootstrap.sh` currently emits (the behaviour).
- AMEND 3 — the gap demonstration is a deliverable: record the guard **red** on the unfixed tree
  **and** `make check` green in that same state.
- AMEND 4 — per-assertion mutation notes; the "distinct from `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`" assertion is
  load-bearing (`services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:133` refuses to start on equality).

#### Files (superseding the draft's list)

| file | why |
|---|---|
| `scripts/env-bootstrap.sh` | add `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN` to the opaque-token loop — its own draw |
| `scripts/check-required-env.sh` *(new)* | the guard: compose `:?` set minus generated set, Docker-free |
| `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` | `expect_pass` clean baseline + `expect_fail` on the deleted generation line |
| `scripts/browser.sh` | correct the false "in-Docker scanner build is broken (TKT-227)" comment |
| `docs/demo-readiness.md` | fold in the resolved diagnosis; drop the "optionally correct TKT-227" item |
| `docs/learnings/2026-08-07-a-failed-optional-dependency-is-skipped-silently.md` | record both diagnoses |
| `docs/LEARNINGS.md` | index entry |
| `docs/development.md` | document the credential beside the others |

Dropped from the draft's list: `scripts/env-bootstrap-test.sh` (replaced by
`scripts/check-required-env.sh` + the selftest seed) and the `Makefile` `check-env-bootstrap`
target (decision 2). `compose.smoke.yaml` and `scripts/stack-env.sh` stay untouched — correct today.

#### Definition of done

- `make up` reaches a healthy stack from a `.env` lacking the token (port overrides allowed, per
  pre-mortem 3 — that is a documented box-local Docker Desktop/WSL2 issue, not this ticket).
- The guard goes **red** on the unfixed tree with `.env` absent, and **green** after the repair,
  both captured.
- `make check` green — and explicitly noted as *not* evidence for this ticket (pre-mortem 2).
- `./scripts/gate-selftest.sh` green, including the new seed.
- No credential value is ever printed by the guard or the test.
- ADR-009: no generated code is touched, so `check-generate` has nothing to commit; verified rather
  than assumed. ADR-035 does not bind — no dependency version moves, and `check-dep-drift` is
  Go-module-only.

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Carried forward from the critique, unchanged and still true at Gate 2 — these three reached this
point reviewed by nobody but their author (me):

1. **The Docker-free compose-parse mechanism.** Known weakness, stated: it reads `${VAR:?}`
   literally, so a requirement expressed via `env_file` or split across lines would be invisible.
   All 19 current requirements use this exact form. **Mitigation now folded into the plan:** the
   guard fails loudly if it parses **fewer than 19** required variables, so the parser silently
   matching nothing cannot read as a pass — the *a-precondition-that-cannot-fail* trap from
   AGENTS.md.
2. **Dropping the `make check` target** in favour of the existing selftest seam.
3. **The invariant sentence** in AMEND 2.

### Adversarial review — by `gpt-5.6-luna` (config.models.aiReview), two passes

Cross-model invariant holds: implemented by `main-agent`, reviewed by `gpt-5.6-luna`. Both passes
ran against the branch diff with **no plan and no rationale supplied** — the reviewer was primed to
assume the diff is wrong and find where. Both returned conclusive verdicts with code-cited findings
(each announced a local skill first; per `codex-runner.md` the rubric is irrelevant when the
findings are concrete).

#### Pass 1 — `origin/main..f13db105` → **needs-attention**, 2 findings, both ACCEPTED

| # | severity | finding | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | high | Name-only comparison accepts **empty** required credentials | **fixed** |
| 2 | medium | Requirement discovery misses the `${VAR?}` form | **fixed** |

Both **verified by execution before fixing**, not accepted on the reviewer's authority:

```
${VAR:?} with VAR="" → error while interpolating … is missing a value   # empty IS rejected
${VAR?}  with VAR="" → X: ""                                            # empty is NOT rejected
${VAR?}  with VAR unset → error … is missing a value                    # a real required form
```

That is a genuine [high]: my guard compared **names**, so `INVENTORY_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN=` would have
reported "all 19 generated" while `make up` still died — the exact defect the guard exists to
prevent, wearing a different hat. **This is the shape AGENTS.md warns about** (a green check that
cannot reach the failing state), and I did not catch it; the cross-model pass did. I had
independently found the empty-value gap while probing, but had **not** found the `${VAR?}` form.

Fix: the generated side now reports `NAME<TAB>set|empty`, requirements are classified
`strict` (`:?`) vs `loose` (`?`), and emptiness is judged against the form that requires it. Names
are matched in Compose's character class rather than uppercase-only. Names and reasons are printed;
values never are.

#### Pass 2 — `f13db105..HEAD`, the **fix diff** → **needs-attention**, 1 finding, ACCEPTED

Earned: pass 1 fixed a blocking [high] and rewrote parse control flow, so the fix diff was code
nobody had reviewed.

| # | severity | finding | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | medium | The scan counted `${VAR:?}` inside **YAML comments** and inside `$${VAR:?}` (Compose's literal escape) | **fixed** |

Verified against Compose before fixing — a config with both, variables unset, resolves cleanly. Not
reachable in `compose.yaml` today (no such occurrence exists), but the failure *direction* is the
one that matters: it would invent a missing credential and **fail the gate on a valid stack**, and a
strict occurrence in a comment could upgrade a real loose requirement through strict-wins. Fixed by
stripping comments and `$$` escapes before classification. Still exactly **19** requirements
afterwards, so the stripping swallowed no real one.

Pass 2 **explicitly cleared** the things I asked it to attack hardest and found sound: the awk
hash-iteration and strict-wins dedup, the generated-side value/quote parsing, the `NR==FNR` join,
secret leakage through the new paths, and the isolation of seeds 9b/9c (`git checkout -- .` runs
between seeds, so none can pass on a predecessor's leftover mutation).

#### Second pass called; no third

Two passes on a stable diff, and the diff **converged** — 2 findings → 1, each pass refuting
something real, and pass 3's fix is a tokenizer filter plus an `expect_pass` seed. No churn (nothing
re-litigated, no already-triaged finding resurfaced). Stopping at the cap by rule.
